Order of Application for condonation of delay.

The instant criminal revision has been filed against the impugned order dated 18.05.2015 passed by learned Principal Judge Family Court, Kanpur Dehat under Section 125 Cr.P.C. in Maintenance Case No.248 of 2013, Police Station Bhognipur, District Kanpur Dehat.

entities.text: Principal Judge Family Court, Kanpur Dehat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Whereby the family court has awarded maintenance at the rate of Rs.2,500/- per month from the date of order to the applicant,
who is respondent No.2 in present Criminal Revision.

Heard Sri Anurag Dubey, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Umesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Prashant Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and perused the material available on record.

Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that as per report of Stamp Reporting Section the Pushpendra @ Anshu vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168899821/
1 revision is delayed by 2487 days i.e. around eight years and six months.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the same has been explained in affidavit accompanying the application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of Limitation Act.

He next submitted that the impugned order passed by learned Family Court on 18.05.2015 could not be acted upon due to compromise entered between the parties on 27.06.2016 before the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Bhognipur District Kanpur Dehat.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate, Bhognipur District Kanpur Dehat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The statement was given by respondent No.2 in said Complaint Case No.334 of 2012, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC, and Section 3/4 of D.P.
Act, Police Station Bhognipur District Kanpur Dehat to the effect that compromise has been arrived at between the parties and she is no longer interested in prosecuting the criminal case, and therefore the complaint case may be dismissed in light of compromise.

entities.text: Police Station Bhognipur District Kanpur Dehat
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However, no final order could be passed in the said criminal case on the basis of compromise .
He next submitted that after the compromise in the year 2016, both husband and wife started living together at the place of husband till, 2019.
Thereafter respondent No.2 again left her matrimonial home and filed application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. for execution of said maintenance order on 01.04.2019.

Learned court below issued recovery warrant against the revisionist on 03.04.2024 and thereafter when the revisionist came to know about the issuance of said recovery warrant he has filed present defective criminal revision.

The delay occasioned in filing the present criminal revision is not deliberate, due to the fact that compromise has been arrived at between the parties in the year 2016,
and respondent No.2 left the place of revisionist on her own volition.
He could be able to prosecute the maintenance case only when he was apprised of issuance of recovery warrant by the Court below on 03.04.2024.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that revisionist never complied the maintenance order passed by the learned court below in said maintenance case and deliberately avoided its compliance at least he should have complied the maintenance order in the year 2019,
when parties again parted their ways.
He has not paid a single penny towards maintenance and recovery warrant has already been issued by the court below for realisation of amount of maintenance.
The revisionist was always in the knowledge of maintenance order, and such inordinate delay finds no plausible explanation.

He further submitted that inasmuch as the revisionist has already filed an application under Section 125 (5) Cr.P.C. and also under Section 127(2)(3) Cr.P.C. on 30.10.2019 before the family court for setting aside the impugned order and inspite of filing an application before the court below, the present revision has been filed to thwart execution proceedings started in 2019, which is nothing but an application for proceedings for the same cause before the two courts.

Inspite of main problem faced by respondent No.2 she made every effort to adjust with the revisionist, but latter again kicked her out from his house in the month of January, 2018 when she was carrying three months pregnancy.
She is living at her parental place since then alongwith her baby daughter Trisha who born in the month of May 2018.
Due to non-compliance of maintenance order it is difficult for the respondent No.2 to make her both ends meet.
Revisionist has also filed a divorce petition under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act, before family court.

The reasons as well as application condonation of delay is not bonafide and deserves to be dismissed.

Considering the rival submissions made by the parties and the grounds taken in the application for condonation of delay and counter affidavit filed in objection to grounds taken in application for condonation of delay, the inordinate delay of 2487 days i.e. eight years and six months in filing the present revision and the admitted fact that revisionist was in the knowledge of said impugned judgment and order for long period.
I am of the considered opinion that the revisionist has failed to explain the delay sufficiently and no good grounds for condonation of delay has been putforth by him before this Court.
The application for condonation of delay deserves to be dismissed.
The application is accordingly dismissed.
Consequently the present criminal revision is also dismissed.
